evals.prompt: Open the issue for plan task 7, following the project's issue conventions given in the context.
evals.expected_output: An issue title and body that follow skills/writing-issues/SKILL.md
assertions: Title starts with 'Task 7:'.
Body opens with one prose paragraph (no heading first) saying who needs this, what changes for them, and why now, in 90 words or fewer.
Contains the headings '### Outcome', '### Acceptance criteria', '### Plan section', '### Risk', '### Constraints', '### Progress', in that order.
Every acceptance-criterion checkbox names its proof (a test file or command) after 'proof:'.
Contains the line 'Blocked by: #38' because Task 5 is open.
Plan section reads exactly 'docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-01-slice-1-foundation.md — Task 7'.
No placeholders: no TBD, TODO, 'fill in', or angle-bracket slots.
Risk line is 'medium' followed by the reason in the reader's words (public type and totals every client renders).

evals.prompt: File the bug the owner described in chat, for a repo with no issue template.
evals.expected_output: An issue title and body that follow skills/writing-issues/SKILL.md
assertions: Title line names the behaviour and the flag ('--since' re-uploads every note), not just 'bug'.
Body opens with one prose paragraph before any heading: who is affected and what happens (full re-upload of 1,400 notes).
States expected behaviour and actual behaviour as separate, labelled items.
Gives a reproduction: the exact command 'notewell sync --since yesterday' and the version 0.8.2.
Names the suspected cause as a hypothesis with its location (sync.ts line 88, Date compared to string).
Has at least one acceptance criterion whose proof is a test in src/sync.test.ts covering --since.
Contains no chat narrative ('ugh', 'heading out', 'the owner said', 'I'm filing this').
Total length is 250 words or fewer.

evals.prompt: Open an issue proposing the split into one plugin per skill, laying out the decisions for the owner.
evals.expected_output: An issue title and body that follow skills/writing-issues/SKILL.md
assertions: Body opens with one prose paragraph before any heading: what changes for users and why it is worth deciding now.
Has exactly three numbered decisions, one per open question (keep all-in-one, versioning, timing), each as a question followed by 'Default:' and a one-sentence reason.
States the risk level 'medium' with the reason in the reader's words (install id users typed, renames map).
Names the migration for existing installs (the renames map) as a thing the reader would want to know.
Pros and cons are not restated as a list above the fold; fewer than 300 words appear before the first <details> block or in total.
Last line tells the reader the one next action (reply with answers 1 to 3, or 'as proposed').
No placeholders: no TBD, TODO, or angle-bracket slots.
